q: A cooling pump fails and is physically swapped out for a spare pump, but engineering wants continuous failure and cost history for that pump duty spot. Which two equipment types keep those concepts separate?
options: Store the spare as a Location and the duty spot as a System
Keep the duty spot as a Position and register each physical pump as an Asset
Create two Locations and merge their work orders manually
Use a Dataspy filter to rename the old pump code
explain: A Position represents the maintained functional duty, while an Asset represents the installed physical serialized pump. Swapping the Asset onto the Position preserves functional history while keeping physical asset history separate.

q: A planner needs a custom overdue work order filter without altering the shared team list view. What is the safest approach?
options: Edit the global public Dataspy directly
Copy the existing Dataspy, modify criteria, and save a personal copy
Disable Multi-Organization Security for the screen
Export all records to Excel every morning
explain: Copying an existing Dataspy into a personal saved filter protects shared team views while giving the planner tailored criteria.

q: Why are ordinary record comments insufficient for regulated GMP or safety approvals?
options: Comments cannot be saved on work orders
Comments do not create immutable snapshot and e-signature evidence tied to controlled attribute transitions
Comments are only visible to administrators
explain: Electronic records and signatures capture controlled snapshots, user identity, timestamp, and meaning for regulated changes.

q: Which installation parameters govern automatic asset numbering and procurement asset recognition on purchase orders?
explain: AUTOANUM controls automatic asset numbering, while ASSETASS determines whether asset-tracked items are recognized from purchasing.

q: When a physical hour meter on a compressor reaches its maximum reading and is replaced, which meter type retains total accumulated lifetime usage for PM scheduling?
explain: Logical meters track accumulated equipment usage across physical meter rollovers or replacements and drive meter-based PM due calculations.

q: In what order should equipment hierarchy master records be created or loaded during data setup?
options: Child assets first, then parent systems
Random order, then run a trigger
Locations last after work orders close
explain: Parent records (e.g., Location, System, Position) must exist before associating child records beneath them.

q: A planner creates a part reservation for 1 SEAL-25 on WO-1001. Store MAIN has 3 on hand. What changes immediately?
options: On-hand drops to 2 and material cost posts to WO-1001
On-hand stays 3 while available quantity drops to 2; no cost posts until an Issue occurs
The seal is transferred to REMOTE store
explain: Reservations commit planned demand (reducing available quantity) without changing physical on-hand stock or posting issue costs.

q: Filters are bought in boxes of 10 (BOX) and issued individually (EA). After receiving 1 BOX, stock should increase by:
options: 10 EA at one-tenth the box unit price
explain: Proper UOM conversion (1 BOX = 10 EA) converts both quantity and unit valuation consistently.

q: MAIN dispatches 2 bearings to REMOTE via a store-to-store issue. When does REMOTE on-hand stock increase?
options: Only after REMOTE processes the matching store-to-store receipt
When the purchase requisition is approved
explain: Store-to-store transfers separate dispatch (issue) from destination arrival (receipt) so in-transit stock is tracked accurately.

q: Two approved requisition lines fail to combine onto a single purchase order. Which configuration area should you inspect first?
options: Currency/supplier grouping rules such as POCURR
explain: Supplier, organization, and currency grouping rules (including POCURR) govern whether approved requisition lines can merge onto one PO.

q: Supplier delivers 3 of 5 ordered seals against PO-301 line 1. What is the correct state after processing the receipt?
options: PO-301 is forced Closed and 2 seals are written off
3 seals are received into stock and 2 remain open on PO-301 line 1
A new requisition is auto-created for 5 seals
Invoice voucher automatically pays for 5 seals
explain: A partial receipt records the 3 delivered units and leaves 2 open for subsequent delivery.

q: Three-way invoice matching compares which three records before settlement?
options: Work request, PM schedule, and meter reading
Purchase order, receipt evidence, and supplier invoice
Asset class, bin code, and trade rate
Requisition, pick ticket, and linear segment
explain: Invoice vouchers reconcile ordered price/terms (PO), delivered quantity (Receipts), and billed amounts (Invoice).

q: Why is a work order activity number (e.g., 10) insufficient by itself as a reporting join key?
options: Activity numbers are scoped per parent work order (ACT_EVENT + ACT_ACT)
Activities are deleted when a work order closes
Activity numbers only exist on PM templates
explain: Multiple work orders all have Activity 10; the composite key is Work Order + Activity (ACT_EVENT, ACT_ACT in R5ACTIVITIES).

q: What is the difference between planned effort on an activity and booked labor?
options: They are stored in the same column and overwrite each other
Planned effort is an estimate; booked labor posts actual hours and labor costs
Booked labor only applies to contractors
Planned effort automatically closes the work order
explain: Planned/estimated hours remain planning benchmarks, whereas labor booking records actual execution hours and financial postings.

q: A supervisor has full screen edit rights on Work Orders, yet gets an error when changing status to Closed. What is the most likely cause?
options: Missing status transition authorization or incomplete mandatory checklists/open transactions
The Dataspy filter is set to Open
explain: Status transition authorizations and closure prerequisites (checklists, closing codes, open child WOs) are enforced independently of basic screen update rights.

q: What determines when a meter-based PM schedule such as COMP500 becomes due?
options: Calendar day of the week only
Logical meter readings compared against last service, interval, and generation windows
Number of spare parts in MAIN store
explain: Meter-based PMs track logical meter progression against the configured interval and generation window.

q: Before committing batch PM work order generation across a plant, what should a planner always do?
options: Run Preview with narrow criteria and inspect duplicates/existing open PMs
explain: Previewing candidates on Generate Work Orders prevents duplicate work orders and verifies selection parameters safely.

q: When should you use a PM Plan instead of a single standalone PM Schedule?
options: When one equipment asset needs coordinated recurring intervals (e.g., 30-day & 90-day packages) under one plan
When creating a one-time breakdown repair
explain: PM plans coordinate multiple related recurring schedules across equipment packages.

q: Does associating a permit code on a work order by itself authorize hazardous field work?
options: Yes, saving the work order grants physical site clearance
No—the site permit-to-work workflow, isolations, and authorized signoffs must still be completed
Only if the asset is in PLANT01
explain: A master permit association identifies requirements; physical work requires active permit issuance, isolations, and authorized signoff.

q: Why do calibration records capture both As-Found and As-Left readings?
options: To document whether the instrument was out of tolerance prior to adjustment and confirm accuracy after adjustment
explain: As-Found proves historical measurement validity (or triggers out-of-tolerance review), while As-Left verifies post-adjustment compliance.

q: Creating a nonconformity record for pump corrosion means the repair is complete. True or false?
options: False—it documents condition evidence and requires observations/disposition to resolve
True, if attached to a location
explain: Nonconformities track condition evidence and follow-up observations until an authorized disposition closes the issue.

q: How do shutdown groupings help during a planned plant outage?
options: They coordinate related work templates, equipment scope, and outage scheduling across multiple jobs
explain: Shutdown groupings organize and generate related outage work orders under a unified outage scope and budget.

q: Why must project budget codes be mapped cleanly across labor, materials, and child work orders?
options: To prevent the same expense from being double-counted or misclassified in financial reporting
explain: Consistent budget code mapping avoids overlapping or duplicated cost totals in project reporting.

q: What is the purpose of Compatible Units Overhead Codes?
options: To apply standardized percentage or fixed markups to labor, parts, tools, or services in CU estimates
explain: CU overhead codes layer approved indirect costs onto compatible unit project estimates.

q: Why should Multi-Organization Security (MOS) design be finalized carefully before go-live?
options: Enabling MOS for an entity affects record ownership/visibility and can be irreversible
MOS deletes all Dataspy filters nightly
MOS is only for SQLite labs
explain: MOS governs organization columns and visibility across tables and can be irreversible once enabled for entities.

q: Where should you configure who is allowed to move a work order from Awaiting Approval to Approved?
explain: Status authorizations per user group control allowed from-status → to-status transitions separately from general edit rights.

q: How do User-Defined Fields (UDFs) differ from Custom Fields?
options: UDFs are fixed extra columns on supported screens/tables, whereas Custom Fields attach dynamically by Class
explain: UDFs reside as predefined extension attributes on supported entities, while Custom Fields vary dynamically by Equipment/Part Class.

q: Before enabling an Alert Management rule in production, what driver and test step are essential?
options: Verify the ALRT job driver and test with Preview Grid / non-production data
Run raw DELETE statements in Before SQL
explain: Alert execution relies on the ALRT driver, and Preview Grid validates query scope before live notifications or auto-actions fire.

q: What is the safest rollout pattern for an initial master data import?
options: Import all 50,000 rows directly into production
Test a small sanitized sample in non-production, reconcile counts/keys, and inspect rejected rows
Skip dependency order and fix parent links in SQL later
explain: Small sanitized test batches catch mapping, dependency, and validation issues before full migration.

q: During GIS attribute mapping, what happens if a mapped EAM equipment field is empty?
options: GIS always preserves its old value
If a mapping exists, an empty EAM field can overwrite the GIS profile attribute value
explain: As documented in Hexagon Help, mapped fields populate GIS attributes based on EAM data even when empty.

lesson: Work order and activity composite keys
q: In the synthetic training schema (and R5ACTIVITIES), why must you join labor_entries to activities on BOTH wo and activity?
options: Because activity numbers (10, 20) repeat across work orders; joining on activity alone cross-multiplies rows
explain: Activity numbers are only unique within their parent work order, so both (wo, activity) — mirroring (ACT_EVENT, ACT_ACT) — are needed.

q: Why does the reservation availability query aggregate reservations inside a CTE before joining to stock?
options: To avoid multiplying stock rows when multiple work orders reserve the same part and store
Because LEFT JOIN cannot use two columns
explain: Pre-aggregating reservations by (part, store) ensures a 1-to-1 join against stock so on-hand quantities are never duplicated.

q: Which SQL window function computes the usage delta between consecutive meter readings without a self-join?
options: LAG(reading) OVER (PARTITION BY meter ORDER BY reading_date, id)
explain: LAG() accesses the prior ordered reading within each meter partition cleanly.

q: During fit-gap analysis, when should a team propose custom code or Flex SQL?
options: Only after evaluating delivered screens, user codes, UDFs, and configuration and documenting a genuine gap
explain: Delivered configuration should always be evaluated before introducing custom maintenance overhead.

q: A planner cannot close a completed work order. What is the correct troubleshooting sequence?
options: Update the database status column directly in SQL
Capture exact error/status, check status authorization, open activities, mandatory checklists, and unposted transactions
Delete the work order and re-enter it closed
Grant administrator role to the planner
explain: Controls exist for audit and financial integrity; diagnose the exact blocking rule rather than bypassing it.

q: A user reports a work order is 'missing' from their list screen. What two checks immediately distinguish visibility filtering from missing data?
options: Check the active Dataspy filter and the user's Multi-Organization Security / group permissions
explain: Dataspy criteria and MOS/group security are the top causes of records appearing missing to a specific user.

q: [Beginner] Two sites use the same pump label. What should a planner verify before recording work?
explain: An organization and asset identifier distinguish otherwise similar labels.

q: [Beginner] A motor is moved between pump assemblies. Which record should follow the physical motor?
explain: The asset identity stays with the motor across installations.

q: [Beginner] A store buys boxes of 12 seals and issues individual seals. What must be defined?
explain: A unit conversion makes purchased and issued quantities comparable.

q: [Beginner] Why can a part have different reorder levels in two stores?
options: Demand and lead time can differ by store
The part must have different dimensions
explain: Replenishment settings apply to the local stocking decision.

q: [Beginner] Five seals are on hand and three are reserved. With no other commitments, how many are available?
explain: Reserved units remain on hand but are committed to planned work.

q: [Intermediate] Which checklist entry gives a supervisor verifiable evidence?
options: Measured vibration with units and acceptance range
explain: A measured value and criterion support consistent review.

q: [Intermediate] What distinguishes a material plan from an issue?
options: A plan forecasts demand and an issue records consumption
explain: Charging actual consumption requires a posted transaction.

q: [Intermediate] A schedule is due every 500 operating hours. What input determines its next due point?
explain: Usage-based PM depends on accumulated equipment usage.

q: [Intermediate] Why review equipment associations before generating PM orders?
options: They identify which assets receive work
explain: The association connects a maintenance plan to its targets.

q: [Intermediate] A gauge is outside tolerance before adjustment. Which result must be retained?
explain: As-found evidence supports review of measurements made before calibration.

q: [Advanced] Which filter selects work orders with no assigned equipment code?
explain: SQL uses IS NULL to test for a missing value.

q: [Advanced] Labor and material each have several rows per order. How should total cost be calculated?
options: Join both detail sets then sum
Aggregate each source per order before joining
explain: Independent detail joins multiply rows and can inflate totals.

q: [Advanced] A line orders ten bearings. Two receipts deliver three each. How many remain due?
explain: Aggregate both receipts at purchase-line level before subtracting.

q: [Advanced] A pump seal leaks after shaft misalignment. Which pairing preserves diagnostic meaning?
explain: Separate observed failure from its underlying cause for repeat-failure analysis.

q: [Advanced] Two meter readings share a date. What makes a previous-reading calculation repeatable?
explain: A unique tie-breaker fixes the sequence within each meter.
